paper_of_the_week.title: Sex-related differences after ACL reconstruction differ between early functional recovery and 5-year outcomes.
paper_of_the_week.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
paper_of_the_week.clinical_summary: This retrospective cohort study addresses Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation. The reported population was: analyzed according to sex The intervention or exposure was: primary ACLR between January 2017 and December 2019, with standardized 6-month functional and psychological assessment and available 5-year follow-up No clear between-group advantage was reported.
paper_of_the_week.practitioner_takeaway: This study may meaningfully inform practice in Ligament and return-to-sport rehabilitation. No clear between-group advantage was reported. Full-text review should still confirm the methods, intervention details, comparator, effect magnitude, adverse events, and applicability to the patient population.
paper_of_the_week.research_takeaway: Future studies should address the identified reporting and methodological limitations, particularly around effect estimates, precision, confounding, and clinical importance where applicable.
major_cautions: The retrospective design increases the risk of selection bias and incomplete data.
Retrospective data may contain selection bias, missing data, and uncontrolled confounding.
Clinical importance or a minimally important difference is not clearly discussed.

specialist_takeaways.sports_performance: The study is relevant to Strength, Recovery, Return to sport. Sports-performance confidence is high. Transfer to competitive athletes depends on training status, intervention specificity, outcome validity, and similarity to real competition demands.
specialist_takeaways.womens_athlete_health: This paper addresses Female injury risk. Women's-athlete-health confidence is high. Interpretation should consider whether female participants were adequately represented, whether sex-specific analyses were performed, and whether menstrual, hormonal, bone-health, and training variables were measured appropriately.
